items.title: Anthropic Releases and Temporarily Suspends Claude Fable 5
items.summary_1line: On June 9, 2026, Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5, a model designed for long-horizon tasks, but it was taken offline shortly after due to a U.S. government export directive. It shares architecture with Claude Mythos...
items.editor_note: Outside recap; first to frame the suspension as temporary and tie it to a US export-control directive.

editorial.tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the higher Mythos 5 tier in mid-June, billing the Mythos-class model as made safe for general use, though launch coverage immediately flagged controversial usage terms; an early hands-on found Fable 5 "relentlessly proactive." Then on Jun 13 the story turned: a US government export-control directive, citing national security, suspended access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and industry coverage reframed the launch as models deemed too dangerous to release. A later recap framed the takedown as a temporary suspension.
editorial.whats_new: An outside recap from InfoQ is the first to characterize the takedown as a temporary suspension — tying it to a US export-control directive — rather than a permanent pull.
editorial.why_it_matters: A top-tier model can go from general-availability launch to government-ordered suspension within days, and even a 'temporary' status leaves re-enablement uncertain.
editorial.take_for_builders: A flagship can go GA → government-suspended in days. Keep a fallback model wired in rather than hard-coding a single flagship tier into production.

status.detail: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launched "made safe for general use," then a US export-control directive pulled access on national-security grounds. Latest framing: the takedown is a temporary suspension, not a permanent pull.
